finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml::`allowed_bots` hardcodes the bot login "yorkie-agent" with nothing tying it to the app actually configured via agent_app_id; if the slug differs the allow-list silently fails to match and every fix run still aborts
evidence: The supplied files confirm the mechanics of the claim: `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` is a literal string (agent-review-panel.yml ~line 413, agent-iterate-ci.yml ~line 160) while the App identity comes solely from `secrets.AGENT_APP_ID` / `secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` in the `Generate GitHub App token` steps, and the design doc (harness-engineering.md, threat-model section) speaks generically of "the Claude GitHub App" / "the write-capable App token" without pinning a slug. None of the other supplied workflow files (agent-implement.yml, agent-review-reply.yml) or scripts reference `yorkie-agent`, so nothing in the visible tree asserts or validates that the installed App's slug matches the allow-list; `actions/create-github-app-token` does expose an `app-slug` output that would make this derived. The defect is therefore real as a brittle, unverified coupling — but it is contingent (it only bites when the deployed App's slug differs) and fails safe rather than dangerously: the fix job errors and the newly added `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` branch of `stalled` pages a human instead of the loop silently proceeding. I could not grep the actual repo (no checkout) or see the withheld task doc, so I cannot confirm the repo-wide grep claim or what App the maintainer actually installed, hence medium confidence.
